thread:
alex_support: FYI — ACME reported their monthly credits 'refilled' ~1 hour earlier than they expected after yesterday's timezone shift. They hit 429s and think the refill moved. Logs attached below from their side.

alex_support: excerpt from customer logs:
```
2026-03-28T07:02:12+01:00 GET /v1/embeddings 429 r=rid_aa12
2026-03-28T07:05:30+01:00 GET /v1/embeddings 429 r=rid_aa13
2026-03-28T07:31:01+01:00 GET /v1/embeddings 200 r=rid_aa20
```

alex_support: They say their app expected refill at 08:00 local. Customer timezone: Europe/Berlin (account set to Europe/Berlin in UI). They provided tenant id T-ACME-001.

sophie_billing: Thanks — quick checklist: 1) which timezone is the billing window configured in our system for that tenant (tenant timezone vs billing clock), 2) any ongoing migratory flags for refill window, 3) DST handling bug possible. I'll check billing config.

mike_ops: Paging ops-bot to confirm: do we roll monthly buckets at tenant-local midnight or at a canonical UTC boundary for older tenants? @ops-bot can you show recent refill schedule for T-ACME-001?

ops-bot: Cached schedule for T-ACME-001: refill_cron=0 8 * * * Europe/Berlin (stored) ; effective_rollout=2026-03-28T00:00:00Z ; migration_flag=off ; last_refill=2026-03-28T06:00:00Z UTC

alex_support: ops-bot says last_refill was 06:00 UTC which is 07:00 CET. Customer saw 07:02-07:05 429s which aligns with that. But they expected 08:00 local (which would be 07:00 UTC). Hmm.

sophie_billing: Two things to surface: (A) historical tenants created before 2024-09 used a legacy refill window aligned to UTC 00:00 with a per-tenant offset applied, (B) customers can set "display timezone" in UI — it doesn't change the underlying refill cron if they were on legacy behavior. Might be a mismatch between displayed timezone and refill clock.

mike_ops: Repro steps to confirm: 1) fetch tenant refill cron: `GET /internal/tenants/T-ACME-001/refill` 2) check refill history: `GET /internal/tenants/T-ACME-001/refill/history?limit=5` 3) compare last_refill timestamps to expected local midnight. If values show 06:00 UTC -> refill happened at 07:00 CET.

alex_support: I ran step 1 and attached output; customer-facing UI shows "refill @ 00:00" in their timezone which led to confusion. They think local midnight is 08:00 because they schedule around a different product midnight (their own infra). They want us to align or explain. Customer is on Dedicated trial plan.

sophie_billing: Proposed response to customer: explain that underlying refill uses the tenant's configured refill cron (which for legacy tenants may be stored in UTC with a fixed offset), include exact timestamps of recent refills in both UTC and Europe/Berlin, and offer migration to the new timezone-aware refill behaviour. Also offer to schedule migration during low-traffic window. :+1:

mike_ops: I'll open an ops ticket to (1) verify migration tool will not double-credit during transition, (2) ensure no refill duplicate if we migrate mid-cycle. tagging eng-oncall if needed.

alex_support: Thanks. Customer asked for interim mitigation — is there a way to temporarily increase burst/budget allowance for next 2 hours to avoid 429s tonight if refill remains misaligned?

sophie_billing: We can create a one-off top-up for the tenant (manual credit) or enable temporary grace window in rate limiter for that tenant for N minutes. I'll coordinate with billing to do a manual top-up + ops to relax limiter for 2 hours. Will update when done.

mike_ops: Filing OP-11234: "Tenant refill timezone mismatch — T-ACME-001" and will include these logs and proposed mitigation. Assign to eng-infra for migration validation.

alex_support: Awesome, I'll notify the customer and ask if they'd prefer manual top-up or scheduled migration. Closing loop later with final action. :wave:
